rules.evidence: A user can understand today's small commitments, complete or reopen them, and see progress without pressure.
Today's progress and habit list lead; planning tomorrow appears only after completion.
Progress precedes the list and each habit keeps cue, optional streak, checkbox, and result together.
The daily-checklist pattern, DaylightHabitCard, AgentDemoStatus, and shared state owner are reused.
Incomplete, partial, complete, reopened, and streak-hidden states update independently without losing other progress.
Checkbox state and progress update immediately; complete feedback persists and every item can be undone.
In-progress, complete, and dark previews cover Today; runtime completes, reopens, and recompletes a habit.
A user can review recent consistency and confirm whether tomorrow has a saved plan.
The day-by-day timeline leads; Return to today is a clear secondary navigation action.
Each date and completion or planning state remain paired in chronological context.
AgentDemoSurface provides a consistent adaptive timeline row and the app shell owns navigation.
History and with-plan states derive from today's completion and the persisted tomorrow plan.
A saved plan appears as a Tuesday row and Return to today updates the selected destination.
History and planned previews cover both layouts; runtime arrives after saving and verifies Tuesday.
A reflective user can notice useful patterns without turning them into another completion task.
Weekly completion leads; strongest rhythm and gentle consistency add supporting interpretation.
Each signal now has its own label and value rather than three identical status messages.
A page-local insight composition reuses AgentDemoSurface because its contract does not repeat outside Insights.
This read-only reflection surface derives current counts and exposes no unsupported actions.
No mutation requires page feedback; destination selection communicates arrival and exit.
The production Insights page has both layout previews and runtime navigation coverage.
Mina can choose how Daylight reminds and motivates her without changing committed habits.
Support style preferences lead; identity and weekly progress provide relevant context.
Each preference keeps explanation, switch, and persistent effect in one surface.
AgentDemoProfileHeader and AgentDemoPreferenceSwitch reuse the shared profile and preference contracts.
Reminder and streak visibility are independent controlled states; disabling streaks leaves progress intact.
Adjacent status copy updates immediately and streak visibility changes on Today when the user returns.
Default and quiet profiles cover both layouts; runtime changes streak preference and verifies its status.
After finishing today, a user can intentionally choose tomorrow's habits and reminder.
Habit selection leads to one Save action; the reminder is supporting configuration.
Tomorrow's date, each habit cue, selection, reminder, and selection count appear before saving.
DaylightHabitCard, CharcoalSwitch, CharcoalButton, and the daily-checklist pattern reuse Today behavior.
Selected and unselected habits plus reminder state remain editable; zero selections disable saving.
Checkboxes update immediately and the Save label reports the selected count or recovery requirement.
The deterministic editing state covers both layouts and runtime saves the default three habits.
A planner can confirm what was saved and continue to the place where tomorrow remains visible.
The saved plan result leads and Continue to journey is the single next action.
Habit count and reminder state appear in the result immediately before continuation.
AgentDemoStatus and CharcoalButton provide the same durable-result language as other flows.
The saved state persists tomorrow IDs and reminder choice before navigating to Journey.
Positive persistent feedback states the exact plan and Journey retains it as a dated row.
The saved-result preview covers both layouts and runtime verifies the persistent Tuesday plan.

transitions.trigger: Select Journey or the navigation-bar calendar
Complete today and choose Plan tomorrow

runtimeScenarios.testName: Daylight completes a day and continues into the journey
runtimeScenarios.evidence: The executable widget journey completes and reopens habits, plans tomorrow, verifies the persistent Journey entry, and reviews Insights and Profile preferences.

checks.evidence: Four stable destinations remain selected while tomorrow planning is a focused task with explicit back and completion routes.
Today's commitments lead completion, Journey leads history, Insights leads reflection, and Profile now leads support-style decisions.
Copy is calm, specific to real local behavior, and avoids developer-facing design rationale on secondary pages.
Every meaningful state has compact and standard production previews; timeline rows adapt below 300 logical pixels.
Habits expose labels and checked state, switches expose controlled state, and all navigation and focused-task exits are labeled.
